feedback: No race has run yet, so there is no earlier outcome to cite for this candidate, and this feedback makes no claim about its performance. Your geometry is a symmetric, five-sensor baseline, and I built the controller around it with weights [-2,-1,0,1,2] matched to sensor x, which is what the signal uses to steer. What I had to decide without evidence: base speed (1.8) and gain levels, because I have no speed or steering data from this robot yet. Plan for the next race: if line_loss_events is high or max_error grows on sharp bends, the sensor reach may be too narrow. Try a wider lateral spread (for example x up to plus or minus 0.04 m, within the body limit) before changing the body. If steering_oscillation is high while the robot stays on the line, the wheel_track or forward offset is probably the cause: try a shorter forward offset (y around 0.04 m) to reduce lag, or a wheel_track of 0.10 m to lower turn inertia. If the robot completes with low error, keep the geometry and move to a higher base speed to meet the time limit.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events > 0 on sharp bends: widen the sensor spread to x = -0.04 and 0.04 m (still 5 sensors), keeping sensor_size 0.012, since the baseline outer sensors may be reading flat on the 25 mm tape at high lateral offsets. No earlier race yet supports this; it is a planned response to the next race result.

If steering_oscillation is high with low max_error: shorten the forward offset to y = 0.04 m and reduce wheel_track to 0.10 m, to cut lag and yaw inertia. This is also untested and depends on the next race telemetry.
